- Air drag F_drag ~ (1/2) ρ C_d A v^2. The resulting deceleration a_drag = F_drag/m is smaller for heavier balls (a_drag ∝ A/m).
- So, for the same drop/release conditions, the bowling ball (heavier) loses less speed to drag while falling than the lighter bouncing ball.
- If both had the same e with the ground (same elasticity), the bowling ball would hit the ground faster and bounce back with a larger speed, hence a higher bounce height (ignoring drag after the bounce).

Important caveat:
- Real-world materials matter a lot. A rubber bouncing ball is designed to be very elastic (high e) and will typically bounce much higher than a bowling ball, which is not very elastic. Drag helps the lighter ball even more to lose energy, and the bowling ball’s poor elasticity usually keeps its bounce tiny.
